subject: Life Skills
title: Hot Water vs Cold Water Wash
description: One-minute skill: Hot Water vs Cold Water Wash.

hook.text: About 90% of the energy a washing machine uses goes to heating the water, not spinning clothes.

buildup.text: Hot water opens fabric fibers and dissolves stains faster, but it also fades colors and shrinks cotton.

discovery.text: Modern detergents are formulated to work in cold water. They activate enzymes at low temperatures.

twist.text: Hot water is still needed for towels, bedding, and anything exposed to illness to kill bacteria.

climax.text: Default to cold for daily clothes. Reserve hot for towels, sheets, and heavily soiled items.

punchline.text: Cold saves money and your clothes last longer.

quiz.question: Why is cold water usually sufficient for everyday laundry?
options: Cold water spins the machine faster
Modern detergents activate enzymes in cold water
